title: Hill Stations in Northeast India: Sikkim, Meghalaya, Arunachal and Beyond
seoTitle: Hill Stations in Northeast India and Darjeeling | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: Hill stations of the eastern Himalaya and Northeast India: Darjeeling, Gangtok, Pelling, Shillong, Tawang, Ziro, Kohima, Aizawl and more, with permits and seasons.
description: A guide to the hill stations of the eastern Himalaya and Northeast India: Darjeeling and Kalimpong in West Bengal, Gangtok, Pelling and Lachung in Sikkim, Shillong and Sohra in Meghalaya, Tawang, Dirang and Ziro in Arunachal Pradesh, Kohima in Nagaland, Aizawl in Mizoram and Haflong in Assam, with permit rules, seasons and how to combine them.
dek: The eastern Himalaya and the Northeast's hills combine big views, monasteries, living tribal cultures and some of India's wettest landscapes.
intro: The eastern hills fall into two landscapes. The Darjeeling hills and Sikkim are true Himalaya, with Kanchenjunga on the skyline, tea gardens and Buddhist monasteries. Further east, Meghalaya's plateau, Arunachal's valleys and the Naga and Mizo hills are lower and greener, with strong community cultures.
Darjeeling and Kalimpong are in West Bengal rather than the Northeast, but most travellers combine them with Sikkim, so they are included here.
quickAnswer: The best hill stations in the eastern Himalaya and Northeast India are Darjeeling and Kalimpong in West Bengal; Gangtok, Pelling, Ravangla and Lachung in Sikkim; Shillong and Sohra in Meghalaya; Tawang, Dirang and Ziro in Arunachal Pradesh; Kohima in Nagaland; and Aizawl in Mizoram. March to May and October to December are the best months; Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit for Arunachal, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur.
takeaways: Darjeeling and Sikkim have the clearest Kanchenjunga views from October to December.
Meghalaya is one of the wettest places on earth; visit its waterfalls in or just after the monsoon.
Arunachal, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur require an Inner Line Permit for Indian visitors.
Protected areas in Sikkim, such as Tsomgo and North Sikkim, need permits.
Distances look short on a map but roads are slow; allow full days for transfers.

sections.heading: Permits
list: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur: Inner Line Permit for Indian visitors, available online.
Sikkim: Protected Area Permits for Tsomgo, Nathu La (Indian nationals only) and North Sikkim.
Foreign nationals need Protected Area Permits in several areas; check each state's rules.

sections.heading: Where to stay
paras: Darjeeling and Gangtok have the widest choice, from old tea bungalows and heritage hotels to homestays. In Meghalaya, Shillong makes a good base, with homestays around Sohra for walks to the root bridges. In Arunachal, Tawang, Dirang and Ziro have hotels and homestays, but options are fewer, so book ahead in peak season and around festivals such as the Ziro music festival and the Hornbill Festival in Nagaland.

sections.heading: When to go
list: March to May: rhododendrons and spring flowers; some haze in the lower hills.
June to September: heavy rain, especially in Meghalaya; landslides can close roads.
October to December: the clearest mountain views of the year.
January to February: cold; snow is possible at high places such as Tsomgo, Sela and North Sikkim.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, e-passes and pass openings change; check the official portals before you travel.
Carry warm layers even in summer; nights in the hills are cool.
Carry printed and digital copies of permits and ID.
packing: Warm layers for Sikkim and Tawang

faqs.q: Which is the best hill station in Northeast India?
faqs.a: Gangtok, Shillong and Tawang are the most popular; Darjeeling, just outside the Northeast, is often combined with Sikkim.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to visit hill stations in the Northeast?
faqs.a: Indian visitors need an Inner Line Permit for Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Mizoram and Manipur; parts of Sikkim need Protected Area Permits.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see Kanchenjunga?
faqs.a: October to December usually has the clearest skies.

faqs.q: Can I combine Darjeeling and Gangtok?
faqs.a: Yes, they are about four hours apart by road.

faqs.q: Is Meghalaya good in the monsoon?
faqs.a: The waterfalls are at their best, but trails are slippery and roads can be disrupted.

faqs.q: Which northeastern hill station is best for a first visit?
faqs.a: Shillong or Gangtok: both have good connections, a range of stays and plenty to see within a day's drive.
